{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=autonomous+goal+formation+intrinsic+motivation+objective+discovery+reinforcement+learning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1109/icdl53763.2022.9962187\", \"title\": [\"Getting Priorities Right: Intrinsic Motivation with Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/icdl53763.2022.9962187\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 9, 12]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.70675/6f863351zdd37z4da4z9fa2z5ceed27ddd07\", \"title\": [\"Learning increasingly complex skills through deep reinforcement learning using intrinsic motivation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Apprentissage de compétences de plus en plus complexes via l'apprentissage profond par renforcement en utilisant la motivation intrinsèque</jats:title>\\n                <jats:p xml:lang=\\\"fr\\\">En apprentissage par renforcement (RL), un agent apprend à résoudre une tâche en interagissant avec son environnement. Aﬁn de faire passer à l’échelle ces agents sur des tâches complexes, les méthodes récentes ont proposé avec succès d’intégrer les méthodes d’apprentissage profond au RL, créant le domaine d’apprentissage profond par renforcement (DRL). Cependant, la signiﬁcation sémantique d’une tâche est toujours pourvue par une fonction de récompense experte qui guide l’agent dans son processus d’apprentissage. Ce paradigme contraste avec la manière dont les animaux et humains apprennent: les travaux de psychologie suggèrent que les humains sont intrinsèquement motivés à acquérir de nouvelles connaissances à propos de leur environnement. Dans cette thèse, notre objectif est d’étudier comment la motivation intrinsèque permet de résoudre les problèmes expérimentés par le DRL. Tout d’abord, nous mettons en évidence comment les motivations intrinsèques actuelles attaquent certains problèmes du DRL. Nous classiﬁons et formalisons les méthodes, puis analysons leurs limites. Aﬁn d’exhiber leur importance, nous mettons en avant que ces verrous peuvent empêcher un agent d’apprendre des compétences et représentations de l’environnement de plus en plus complexes. Ce sont des éléments-clés pour faire apprendre des agents autonomes comme des humains. Á partir de cette analyse, nous introduisons deux nouveaux modèles qui…

{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=autonomous+goal+formation+intrinsic+motivation+objective+discovery&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Evolution of University Students' AI Dependency and Creativity in the Technology Diffusion Process: A Four-Wave Repeated Cross-Sectional Study in China.\", \"abstract\": \"Generative artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping higher education, yet potential risks accompany over-reliance on these tools. Grounded in Rogers' diffusion-of-innovations theory, the present study employed a mixed-methods design. Four waves of independent cross-sectional quantitative data (T1-T4, N = 788) were complemented by semi-structured interviews with 20 undergraduate students. Key patterns emerged as follows: (i) Across later waves, the direct association between external regulation and intrinsic motivation attenuated, while the indirect association operating via identified regulation strengthened. The path from identified regulation to intrinsic motivation was the only relationship that demonstrated significant cross-pair differences while satisfying invariance requirements for all three wave-pair comparisons. Because scalar invariance could not be established, this pattern is interpreted solely as a descriptive group-level temporal trend and should not be read as evidence of intra-individual change. (ii) AI-assisted creativity showed the largest and most consistent downward shift: estimates in later waves were significantly lower relative to the T1 baseline, with effect sizes increasing progressively (Δ = -0.391 to -0.549; d = -0.61 to -0.95; all p < 0.001 following Holm correction). This pattern remained largely unchanged after adjusting for gender, year of study, and academic major, and held up in four predefined subsamples as well as under propensity-score weighting. (iii) The linkage between AI dependency and creativity was significantly positive only at T3 and became negative but non-significant at T4, pointing to a conditional, wave-specific association rather than a stable linear relationship. (iv) Observed wave-level differences for AI dependency and intrinsic motivation did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. Sensitivity tests yielded only two significant …
